articles.title: iPhone Duo orders limited to two per customer as Apple tackles scalping
articles.summary: Apple is limiting iPhone Duo purchases to two per customer across markets including the US, UK, Japan, and Spain after shipping dates quickly slipped into January 2027. The restriction applies regardless of configuration and appears designed to reduce scalping, with resellers already listing devices for more than $5,000. Purchase limits cannot eliminate organized scalping entirely, but they could make bulk buying more difficult and improve availability for regular customers.

articles.title: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol
articles.summary: Figma is adding 20 MCP partners even as co-founder Dylan Field argues that the protocol favors frontier AI labs and needs improvement. He says the company wants people to use their Figma data but must limit exposure to reduce potential abuse. Field also pointed to unequal sharing of context across platforms and said Figma plans to support the open-source tool Pi.

articles.title: Bluesky Expands its AI-Powered Attie App to Let Anyone Build Websites, Games, and More
articles.summary: Bluesky's experimental Attie platform now lets everyday users build websites, quizzes, games, and polls, experiences that previously only software developers could make. CEO Toni Schneider calls it "social vibe coding," with creations tied to ATProto identities and able to reach Bluesky's 47 million registered users. Support for private data, the top developer request, is in alpha with a rollout planned by year's end.

articles.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era
articles.summary: Treating UI as a pure function of state lets developers see how a screen varies across roles, plans, billing statuses, and flags, which matters more now that agents take on front-end implementation work. In a worked example, an agent that tested only an owner account reported success on a delete action, yet viewers still saw the button despite a “View only” header. Rendering every state combination side by side exposes such gaps, so teams should make display-relevant state explicit and ask what an agent actually checked before merging.

articles.title: Top Accessibility Errors in Production and How to Avoid Them
articles.summary: Almost 96% of the top million home pages fail at least one automated accessibility check, and the same errors have led WebAIM's report for seven years. Low contrast, missing alt text, unlabeled inputs, and empty links and buttons top the list, each fixable without a rebuild. Automated scans catch only about 30 to 40 percent of issues, so keyboard and screen reader testing still has to happen before release.

articles.title: “You've already proof-tested the answer for years”
articles.summary: A formal design degree is not necessarily required to build a successful creative career when years of experience, skills, self-study, and leadership already demonstrate professional ability. The 70-20-10 learning model suggests that most professional development comes from practical experience and relationships, with formal education accounting for a relatively small portion. Structured courses can still be valuable when they address a specific knowledge gap, build confidence, or support a desired career direction rather than simply validating an already proven career.

articles.title: Digital Accessibility Laws for UX Designers: Which Rules Apply to Your Products
articles.summary: Following accessibility best practices doesn't guarantee legal compliance, and the rules differ across the US, UK, and EU. A four-question check covering market, provider, product type, and exemptions helps identify which of the ADA, Section 508, the European Accessibility Act, and UK laws may apply. Cases involving Domino's, Target, and Fashion Nova show the legal and commercial cost of ignoring them.

articles.title: Does brand design have a longevity problem?
articles.summary: Brands increasingly chase launch-day novelty and short-lived visual trends at the expense of accumulated recognition and long-term usefulness. Durable identities instead build on principles, flexible systems, typography, proportion, composition, and other foundational elements that can evolve without abandoning the equity they have accumulated. Longevity does not require brands to remain visually static, but to preserve their core ideas while adapting their expression to new contexts over decades.

articles.title: HAL Casino is a single-weight serif, sans and mono
articles.summary: HAL Typefaces' HAL Casino combines serif, sans, and monospaced styles within a single-weight family, allowing contrasting typographic voices to work together as one system. Its forms draw on historical serif designs and expressive swash lettering while balancing expressive details with enough consistency for the styles to be mixed freely. The result gives designers multiple distinct textures without requiring them to leave a single coordinated type family.

articles.title: The Hardest Part of Moving from UX to Hardware is Committing
articles.summary: Hardware demands earlier commitment than software, since a released physical product can't be fixed with an update and design choices become costly to reverse.
